entries.title: Numbers 28:1
entries.author: R. A. Torrey (editor)
entries.content: 1 Offerings are to be observed. 3 The continual burnt offering. 9 The offering on the sabbath; 11 on the new moons; 16 at the passover; 26 in the day of the first-fruits.

entries.title: Numbers 28:2
entries.author: R. A. Torrey (editor)
entries.content:
my bread. Le 3:11; 21:6,8; Mal 1:7,12 for a sweet savour unto me. Heb. savour of my rest. 15:3,7,24; Ge 8:21; Ex 29:18; Le 1:9,13,17; 3:11; Eze 16:19 Eze 20:41; *marg: 2Co 2:15; Eph 5:2; Php 4:18 in their due season.The stated sacrifices and service of the tabernacle having, probably, been greatly interrupted for several years, and a new generation having arisen, who were children or minors when the law was given respecting these ordinances; and as they were now about to enter into the promised land, where they must be established and constantly observed; God commands Moses to repeat them to the people in the following order:--1. Daily: the morning and evening sacrifices; a lamb each time. (ver. 3, 4.) 2. Weekly: the sabbath offerings; two lambs of a year old. (ver. 9, 10.) 3. Monthly: at the beginning of each month, two young bullocks, one ram, and seven lambs of a year old, and a kid for a sin offering. (ver. 11-15.) 4. Annual: (1) the Passover to last seven days; the offerings, two young bullocks, one ram, seven lambs of a year old, and a he-goat. (ver. 16-25.) (2) The day of first-fruits: the sacrifices the same as on the beginning of the month. (ver. 26-31.)

entries.title: Numbers 28:27
entries.author: R. A. Torrey (editor)
entries.content: two young. 11,19; Le 23:18,19 Bishop Patrick observes that no peace offerings are appointed in this chapter, which were chiefly for the benefit of the offerers, and therefore in them they were left more to themselves; but burnt offerings, which were purely for the honour of God, and confessions of his dominion, and which figured evangelical piety and devotion, by which the soul is wholly offered up to God, in the flames of holy love; and sin offerings, which were typical of Christ's sacrifice of himself, by which we and our services are perfected and sanctified.
